correctness.rationale: For each vertex (i,t) of C_n Cartesian K_2 the open neighborhood is {(i−1,t),(i+1,t),(i,1−t)}. Pairwise neighborhood overlap yields same-layer separation ±2 or cross-layer ±1. Odd n parity lifting bijects Z/(2n) to vertices, taking step ±1 to cross-layer and ±2 to same-layer; even n splits into two parity components, each C_n squared. Thus vertex-open packings are independent sets of one/two cycle squares. Circular gaps >=3 count each coefficient m/(m−2j) binomial(m−2j,j). Leading coefficients and chromatic forced period-three/explicit 123/1234 constructions prove maxima, counts, injective chromatic number, and perfect partition iff 3|n or n=4,8. Tested the original neighborhood condition exhaustively on 1,398,080 subsets n=3..10 and conflict adjacency n=3..80; finite tests are not substituted for the universal proof.

value.rationale: A natural cubic planar graph family central to prior packing studies has a complete coefficientwise open-packing polynomial rather than merely a maximum bound, with parity-split enumerations and exact counts of all maximizers. It also admits a full classification of perfect injective colorability, including the sporadic exception n=4,8 beyond 3-divisible n. These are natural graph-family invariants, with a structural parity lift and integer partition obstruction supplying mathematical explanation.
